Ellen Trout Zoo announces arrival of baby tapir

By Jeff Awtrey
Published: Oct. 13, 2026 at 5:25 PM EDT
Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:18
Instaread

LUFKIN, Texas (KTRE) - Ellen Trout Zoo in Lufkin is celebrating the birth of Nadira, a female Malaysian tapir.

Nadira was born Sept. 21 at 2:09 a.m. at 20 pounds. She now weighs just over 40 pounds at three weeks old.

Nadira is the third calf born to 10-year-old Tembikai and Cole, who died in January at the age of 24.

Nadira’s name means “precious gift” in Malay.

“Though only a few weeks old, Nadira is already showing off a big personality,” the zoo released in a press statement. “Described by her keepers as full of spunk, she enjoys splashing in her water trough, nibbling on her mother, attempting to steal Tembi’s food, and chewing on just about everything as she begins teething. When she gets a burst of energy, Nadira can even be seen bucking like a little bronco as she races around her surroundings.”

Nadira’s birth is part of the Association of Zoos and Aquariums’ Species Survival Plan, a cooperative program that helps maintain genetically diverse, sustainable populations of threatened and endangered species in accredited zoos.

Nadira can now be seen in an exhibit in holding area No. 2. She will be introduced to the main exhibit when she is able to safely navigate the pool.
